title: Astra Hits the Text Board. The Two-Week Clock Is Still Ticking
excerpt: Astra is on the Sep 13 text board at 1480 Elo. helloai still waits on two weeks and a thicker sample before it can take a slot.
content: The listing last week's article said was missing is now on the board. Arena.ai's September 13, 2026 text-overall snapshot puts gpt-6-astra-max at 1480±12 Elo on 2,693 votes, rank 24. OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra on September 3, so this is a ten-day sample, not two weeks of sustained Elo. helloai's admission rule cares about that distinction more than the rank.

The invoice did not change while the Elo arrived. The API id is gpt-6-astra at $10 input / $50 output per million tokens, cache reads at $1, and a 1,050,000-token context. Prompts over 272K input double input and cache rates and multiply output by 1.5; Fast mode is 2x Standard. Claude Fable 5.1 is the same $10/$50 list with cache reads at $0.25 — four times cheaper than Astra's $1 cache read. A same-sticker competitor with a worse cache still has to clear the Elo gate, not the price sheet.

Code Arena is not the gate, and it already crowned Astra. The September 11, 2026 WebDev board lists gpt-6-astra-max at 1800 on 2,281 votes, rank 1, with claude-fable-5.1-max at 1758 on 3,036 votes. On text overall, Claude Fable 5.1-max is 1498±8 on 5,783 votes, and Muse Spark 1.3-max is now on that board at 1493±9 on 4,723 votes. Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview remains 1487; Qwen3.8-Max is 1481. Astra's 1480 sits a point under Qwen, with a ±12 interval wider than Fable's ±8 and Muse's ±9.

helloai tracks six frontier APIs, and the floor is now Grok 4.6 at 1456 on 15,521 votes, no longer Preliminary. Admission requires LMArena text-overall Elo within 25 points of that floor, sustained two weeks, not a fresh debut with few votes. 1480 clears the 25-point bar versus 1456; 2,693 votes and a ±12 interval on a September 13 snapshot do not clear the two-week / thin-sample bar. Admitting Astra as a new provider would drop Grok — the owner already held GLM-5.3-max at 1483 on 10,960 votes rather than make that cut.

Ten days after ship, the two-week clock is still ticking. The interesting fight is no longer whether GPT-6 Astra has a text Elo. It is whether a 2,693-vote debut at rank 24 is allowed to displace a 15,521-vote floor the table already refused to drop for GLM-5.3-max. If later snapshots keep Astra inside 25 points of Grok 4.6 once that clock runs out, the six-model rule has to name who leaves.

title: Astra Takes WebDev. helloai's Elo Gate Still Holds
excerpt: OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra at Fable's $10/$50. Code Arena WebDev lists it at 1797. helloai still waits on two weeks of text Elo before it can take a slot.
content: OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra on September 3, 2026 at the same $10 input / $50 output per million tokens as Claude Fable 5.1. The API id is gpt-6-astra. Official docs list a 1,050,000-token context window, 128K max output, and cache reads at $1 — four times Fable 5.1's $0.25 cache-read rate. Prompts over 272K input double input and cache rates and multiply output by 1.5 for the whole request. Fast mode is 2x Standard: a Fable-class sticker with a worse cache line.

The independent signal that moved this week is Code Arena, not OpenAI's scorecard. Arena.ai's September 5, 2026 WebDev board lists gpt-6-astra-max at 1797 on 1,199 votes, rank 1. Claude Fable 5.1-max is 1762 on 2,275 votes. Grok 4.6-high is 1625. Muse Spark 1.3 (xHigh) finally has a code-arena slug at 1622. The text-overall snapshot is still dated September 2 — the day before Astra launched — so gpt-6-astra is not on helloai's Elo table yet.

Vendor benches are noisier and should be read as vendor benches. OpenAI reports Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 57.9% for Astra versus 55.8% for Fable 5.1 and 37.3% for GPT-5.6 Sol. It reports ARC-AGI-3 at 99.9% using its own Responses API harness, with a footnote that two settings were changed to match real-world performance. Greg Kamradt of the ARC Prize Foundation said Astra surpassed their human action-efficiency baseline on 96% of levels. Those numbers are why the launch post talks about AGI. They are not why helloai would add a row.

helloai's tracked six is gated on LMArena text-overall Elo, sustained two weeks, with a public API. Astra clears the API and the 200K context bar but fails the Elo bar: it is four days old, the live text board has not listed it, and 1,199 WebDev votes is a debut sample. The set is already at six, so admitting OpenAI as a new provider would force a drop — Grok 4.6 at 1461 is still Preliminary and is the lowest tracked Elo. The owner already held GLM-5.3-max, 1482 on 7,668 votes, rather than drop Grok. Astra does not get a shortcut.

The routing question this week is not whether Astra is good at computers. It is whether a same-price Mythos competitor with a 4x worse cache read belongs on a directory that currently leads coding with Fable 5.1 and daily use with Muse Spark 1.3 at $1.25/$4.25. If the next text-overall snapshot puts Astra inside 25 points of the floor and keeps it there for two weeks, the six-model rule has to name who leaves. Until then, /api/recommend still has no OpenAI row, and the WebDev crown sits on a model the table does not track.

title: Fable 5.1 Cuts Cache Cost While Taking WebDev
excerpt: Claude Fable 5.1 keeps the $10/$50 list but cuts cache reads 75%. Code Arena WebDev lists it at 1765, well ahead of Grok 4.6.
content: Claude Fable 5.1 did not get cheaper on the sticker. Anthropic made it generally available on September 1, 2026 at the same $10 input / $50 output per million tokens as Fable 5, with the same 1M context and 128K max output. The real invoice change is cache reads: $1 down to $0.25 per million tokens, 0.025x base input versus 0.1x on other Claude models. Anthropic estimates typical workloads about 25% cheaper than Fable 5, and highly agentic work up to about 45% cheaper. The API id is claude-fable-5-1.

On arena.ai's September 2, 2026 text overall snapshot, claude-fable-5.1-max sits at 1504±11 Elo on 2,906 votes and is not flagged Preliminary. Predecessor claude-fable-5 is still 1507±5 on 27,189 votes; helloai now tracks 5.1 at 1504. Code Arena WebDev is the bigger shift: claude-fable-5.1-max is 1765, rank 1, while grok-4.6-high is 1629 Preliminary. That ends Grok 4.6's brief WebDev edge over Fable 5, which sat at 1626.

Vendor numbers are noisier and should be treated as vendor numbers. On Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, Fable 5.1 scores 52.6% against Fable 5's 24.7% and Opus 5's 29.0%. On CursorBench 3.2.0, SpaceXAI's Sualeh Asif said Fable 5.1 scored 73.4% at max effort, the highest they had run on that bench. Cognition's Walden Yan said they are moving Devin's Opus 5 traffic to Claude Fable 5.1 on launch day because it matched or edged Fable 5 at lower cost per task, and cheaper cache reads make a Fable-class model economical for workloads they had kept on Opus, starting with code review.

The next day, Meta shipped Muse Spark 1.3 on Muse Code and the Meta Model API at the same $1.25/$4.25 and 1M context as 1.2. Meta says about 20% fewer tool calls and about 25% fewer tokens versus 1.2 in internal comparisons. Max reasoning is not out yet — safety testing. Arena has no 1.3 slug yet, so helloai keeps 1.2 xHigh's 1499 Elo as the fallback.

helloai still tracks six frontier APIs. Fable 5.1 replaces Fable 5; Muse Spark 1.3 replaces 1.2. Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 5, Qwen3.8-Max, and Grok 4.6 are unchanged this week, and Grok 4.6's text overall remains Preliminary at 1461 on 3,453 votes. A same-price successor with a 75% cheaper cache read rewrites routing tables before it rewrites leaderboards. If cache-heavy agent loops keep migrating off Opus-class prices, the interesting split is no longer Fable versus Grok on WebDev — it is which workloads still justify paying Opus once Fable-class cache is this cheap.

title: OpenAI Cuts Sol's Price 20% While It Leads Terminal-Bench
excerpt: OpenAI slashed GPT-5.6 Sol's price 20% the same week it topped Terminal-Bench 2.1 against Opus 5 — an invoice argument for a model helloai's Elo-gated table still leaves off the board.
content: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Sol's price 20% on August 21, 2026 — input from $5 to $4 per million tokens, output from $30 to $20 — and flagged the new rate as promotional through at least November 21. It is the third cut in the GPT-5.6 line in under a month. Terra dropped 20% on July 30. Luna dropped 80% the same day and now lists at $0.20/$1.20. The frontier tier is now being priced like the mid tier was six months ago.

The timing is what makes this interesting rather than routine. Sol posts 89.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, edging Claude Opus 5's 89.1% on the same benchmark. So OpenAI's most expensive current model just got cheaper in the same window it took the lead on an agentic coding benchmark against the model helloai currently ranks as the strongest coder. On raw price-per-capability, that is a real argument, and it is the first one OpenAI has had in a while.

It is not, however, an admission argument. helloai's tracked six is gated on Elo — LMArena head-to-head preference — and nothing else. Sol left the table on July 17 when Kimi K3 replaced it, and Sol was the lowest-Elo entry at the time at 1484. Terminal-Bench measures something narrow and useful: can the model drive a terminal to completion. Elo measures something broad and noisy: do humans prefer the output across everything they happen to ask. A win in the first does not move the second, and the tracked set only reads the second.

There is a wrinkle worth sitting with. The current tracked floor is Grok 4.6 at 1461 — below the 1484 Sol carried when it was dropped. Read one way, that is an inconsistency: the bar moved down after Sol left, and Sol would clear today's floor. Read another way, the July decision was made against July's field, admission is not retroactive, and re-litigating past cuts every time the floor drifts turns a ranked table into a queue of appeals. Neither reading is obviously wrong, which is usually a sign the rule is doing more work than the number behind it.

What the price cut actually changes is the invoice, and that is not nothing — at $4/$20 with a Terminal-Bench lead, Sol is a defensible pick for agentic coding workloads regardless of where it sits on any directory's table. The open question is whether an Elo-gated set should have a price input at all. If cost-per-capability never touches admission, the tracked six will keep describing which model people prefer while saying nothing about which model a team should actually buy. If it does touch admission, the criterion stops being one number and starts being a judgment call. OpenAI has spent a month making that question harder to avoid.

title: Grok Bot Is a Cloud Teammate. The Local CLI Runs the Site
excerpt: Grok Bot, launched August 11, is a cloud teammate with its own VM. The local grok CLI is what can actually operate a production checkout like helloai.
content: xAI is selling two desktop agents this month, and they are not the same product. Grok Bot, launched as an early beta on August 11, 2026, is a macOS, Windows, and iOS app whose Bots share a persistent cloud computer with a browser, filesystem, and terminal. Grok Build is the local grok command: Grok Build 1.0 left beta on August 7, the changelog is at 1.0.5 as of August 15, and the marketing page now says it is powered by Grok 4.6. Calling both Grok Bot is how you confuse a rented VM with the checkout you actually ship from.

Grok Bot's pitch is always-on teammates. Official docs say jobs keep running when you close the laptop, Bots can use apps with no API, and they can watch a workflow once and save it as a routine. Several Bots share one user-scoped cloud computer at /workspace — a convenience and a security boundary. Access is SuperGrok Plus and Heavy, or Cursor Pro+, Ultra, and Teams, signed in with a Cursor account. There is no Linux desktop app. Local-computer execution is a separate setting that defaults to ask-every-time; the computer itself is still in the cloud. That is closer to Claude Cowork than to a repo-native CLI.

A site like helloai.com is a git checkout: data files, tests, a commit, and deploy keys that should not sit on a shared Bot VM. Grok Build is built for that shape. Install is one curl on macOS, Linux, and Windows. It has plan mode, subagents, worktrees, AGENTS.md, skills, hooks, MCP, git, and headless grok -p for scripts. The Apache 2.0 tree is xai-org/grok-build. Claude Code and Codex CLI already occupy this niche. Grok Build is xAI's entry, not a new category.

The trade-offs are not subtle. Cloud Bots work at 3 a.m. and can click a CRM with no MCP server. They require cloud data storage, refuse Cursor's Legacy Privacy Mode, and share logins across every Bot on the account. Local CLIs stop when the session stops unless you wrap them in CI, and they will git push if you let them. Neither is local inference: both call Grok 4.6 in xAI's cloud. The locality is the harness. The weights still leave the building.

This week Grok 4.6 hits two weeks on the public API at $2/$6 with a 500K window. Code Arena WebDev lists grok-4.6-high at 1629, a hair above Claude Fable 5 at 1626; text overall is still Preliminary at 1461. Grok Bot is two weeks old. The useful question for a site like this is no longer whether xAI has a frontier model. It is whether you want the teammate on a computer you rent, or the agent in the directory you already deploy from.

title: Qwen3.8-Max Cools Below Gemini as Arena Votes Arrive
excerpt: Qwen3.8-Max's launch-week arena lead is gone. Two weeks of votes drop it to 1481 Elo, five points under Gemini 3.1 Pro. The $2/$6 card did not change.
content: Qwen3.8-Max is no longer the fourth-ranked model helloai tracks. The arena.ai text-overall snapshot dated August 21, 2026 lists qwen3.8-max at 1481 Elo plus or minus 7 on 9,955 votes. Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview sits at 1486 plus or minus 3 on 99,182 votes. Two weeks ago Qwen was 1491 with 6,908 votes, and the launch-week listing was near 1497. The rate card did not move. QwenCloud still prices the 2.4-trillion-parameter MoE at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output, with a 1M context window. The ranking did.

That is what a thin sample does when it fills in. A plus-or-minus-7 interval on ten thousand votes is still wider than Gemini's plus-or-minus-3 on a hundred thousand, so calling this a settled loss would over-read the board. It is a directional cooling, not a collapse. helloai's August 7 rebalance admitted Qwen3.8-Max because the early arena score sat near 1497, second only to Claude Fable 5 and Muse Spark 1.2 in the tracked set. The same-provider rule that dropped Kimi K3 for Alibaba assumed that launch Elo would hold. It held for a week. It did not hold for two.

The rest of the tracked table barely moved. Claude Fable 5 is 1508, Muse Spark 1.2 is 1498, Claude Opus 5 is 1493, and DeepSeek V4 Pro is still 1458 at $0.66/$1.98 off-peak. Official catalogs for Anthropic, Meta, Google, Alibaba, and DeepSeek show no newer flagship than the rows we already track. Gemini 3.5 Pro is still missing from Google's pricing page. The /api/recommend coding path still surfaces Qwen as the $2/$6 1M option; the Overall Preference order now puts Gemini above it.

The board outside the six-model cap is noisier than the cap itself. Z.ai's GLM-5.3-max, live on the API at the same $1.40/$4.40 as 5.2, already sits at 1487 Elo with 3,751 votes — above Qwen, below Opus 5. Grok 4.6 is still flagged Preliminary at 1461 on 3,473 votes, ten days after launch, with a 500K window that does not beat DeepSeek on price. Neither is auto-admitted this week. Qwen3.8-27B finally has an arena slug at 1440, the signal the open-weight shelf was waiting on, but helloai already carries three Qwen local cards and has no first-party 4090 throughput for the 27B.

The honest read is that Alibaba's Max-class API is a mid-tier frontier row that looks less like a 1497 rocket and more like a 1481 peer of Gemini 3.1 Pro at half the output price. Teams that picked Qwen on August 7 for the Elo, not the invoice, should re-run their own harness rather than the launch table. The next weekly pass is whether GLM-5.3's sample matures at 1487, and whether Grok 4.6's Preliminary flag drops after August 26. Until one of those forces a human replace, the six-model set stays Anthropic, Meta, Google, Alibaba, and DeepSeek — just not in the order the August 7 article sold.

title: DeepSeek Doubled Its Rate Card and Still Leads Daily Use
excerpt: DeepSeek V4 Pro's hike is live today: $0.66/$1.98 off-peak, up from $0.435/$0.87. It remains helloai's cheapest tracked frontier API.
content: DeepSeek's price-leader era just got more expensive. Official API docs put new DeepSeek V4 Pro rates live at 16:00 UTC on August 16, 2026: cache-miss input moves from $0.435 to $0.66 off-peak and $1.32 at peak, and output jumps from $0.87 to $1.98 off-peak and $3.96 at peak. Cache-hit input goes from $0.003625 to $0.022 off-peak and $0.044 at peak. The model id is unchanged — DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 — and arena still lists deepseek-v4-pro at 1458 Elo. The invoice is what changed.

Peak hours are 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, seven hours billed at twice the off-peak rate. helloai lists the off-peak $0.66/$1.98 figure the same way it lists Gemini 3.1 Pro's standard $2/$12. That is still the cheapest tracked frontier API. Muse Spark 1.2 remains $1.25/$4.25, Qwen3.8-Max $2/$6, Gemini 3.1 Pro $2/$12, Claude Opus 5 $5/$25, and Claude Fable 5 $10/$50. Off-peak DeepSeek is about half of Muse on input and output. Peak DeepSeek ($1.32/$3.96) almost meets Muse on input and still undercuts it on output.

The August 7 rebalance sold DeepSeek as an order-of-magnitude undercut of Western mid-tier rates. That sentence is now false. Versus Muse it is a 2x story, not a 10x story. Teams that built agent loops around $0.003625 cache hits will feel the 6x to 12x cache-hit hike more than the headline input bump. Peak windows also sit on a slice of US evening and Asian morning, when a lot of interactive coding agents run. The MIT license and 1M context did not change; the set-it-and-forget-the-bill pitch did.

helloai is not dropping DeepSeek. Honest Daily Use still belongs to the cheapest tracked API with a 1M window, and no other row undercuts $0.66/$1.98. Grok 4.6 is still $2/$6 with a 500K window and a preliminary 1464 Elo — too fresh for the two-week bar, and it does not win on price. Gemini 3.7 Flash shipped August 13 at an introductory $0.75/$3.75, but Flash does not replace 3.1 Pro on hard reasoning, and 3.5 Pro is still missing from Google's pricing page.

The next weekly pass will be about whether anyone else moves. If Muse or Qwen hold their rates, DeepSeek keeps the daily-use slot even after a painful hike. If they cut, or if Grok's arena sample matures above the floor with a unique agent story, the August 7 price-shock admit becomes a one-month footnote. Until then, /api/recommend still routes high-volume, non-Mythos work to DeepSeek — just not at the invoice you budgeted on August 15.

title: Grok 4.6 Ships the Week After helloai Dropped It
excerpt: xAI ships Grok 4.6 today at the same $2/$6 as 4.5, five days after helloai dropped Grok. Arena votes are still too thin to reopen the slot.
content: xAI shipped Grok 4.6 today, five days after helloai dropped Grok 4.5 from the six-model frontier table. Official docs list grok-4.6 at the same $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output that 4.5 charged, with the same 500K-token context window and a $4/$12 surcharge once a prompt crosses 200K. The company recommends it for both chat and code. It is live on the SpaceXAI API plus Cursor, Grok Build, OpenRouter, Vercel, and Cloudflare.

The vendor evals are why 4.6 exists. On xAI's launch table, Grok 4.6 High ties GPT-5.6 Sol Max at 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — one point behind Fable 5 Max at 62 — and lifts CursorBench v3.2 from 66.7 percent on 4.5 High to 69.9 percent. Terminal-Bench v3.0 jumps from 15.7 percent to 26 percent. Those are xAI's numbers, not independent reruns, and DeepSWE v1.1 still trails Sol (65.9 percent versus 73 percent). The pitch is longer agent trajectories and stronger first passes on visual, interactive projects, not a new price or context class.

Arena is the part that keeps 4.6 off helloai's board this week. The text-overall listing for grok-4.6-high sits at 1464 Elo with a plus-or-minus 12 interval and 2,448 votes, marked Preliminary. That is four points below the 1468 we last recorded for Grok 4.5, and it is a fresh debut. Admission requires Elo within 25 points of the tracked floor sustained for two weeks, not a launch-day sample. DeepSeek V4 Pro, which took the slot on August 7, is still the cheapest tracked API at $0.435/$0.87 with 1M context.

helloai is not saying 4.6 is weak. Same-provider upgrades usually replace the prior xAI row automatically; there is no xAI row to replace, because last week's six-model cut went to DeepSeek's price leadership. Re-admitting Grok now would mean dropping someone else — DeepSeek, Gemini 3.1 Pro, or Qwen3.8-Max — without two weeks of arena evidence that 4.6 holds a unique niche at $2/$6. Muse Spark 1.2 still undercuts that rate at $1.25/$4.25.

The first-week 2x included usage in Cursor and Grok Build is the right place to test the agent claims before any directory has to decide. If votes mature and 4.6 stays inside the Elo band while keeping a coding-agent story DeepSeek does not own, the next weekly pass can reopen the human-review question. Until then, /api/recommend keeps DeepSeek as Honest Daily Use and leaves Grok 4.6 as a same-price successor that has not yet earned its row back.

title: Qwen3.8-Max and DeepSeek Join; Grok and Kimi Exit
excerpt: helloai admits Qwen3.8-Max and DeepSeek V4 Pro, drops Grok 4.5 and Kimi K3, and adds gpt-oss-20b to the open-weight shelf under the six-model caps.
content: helloai just re-cut its six-model frontier board and its open-weight shelf in the same pass. Qwen3.8-Max and DeepSeek V4 Pro enter the tracked API set; Grok 4.5 and Kimi K3 leave to hold the six-model cap. On the open-weight side, OpenAI's gpt-oss-20b replaces Qwen3 8B as the local OpenAI pick after first-party cluster benches and arena votes cleared the admission bar.

Qwen3.8-Max is Alibaba's 2.4-trillion-parameter MoE flagship, live on QwenCloud at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output with a 1M-token context window. Arena text overall lists qwen3.8-max near 1497 Elo — third in the refreshed set behind Claude Fable 5 and Muse Spark 1.2. That re-admits Alibaba after July's Muse swap dropped Qwen3.7-Max; the open-weight Qwen3 dense and MoE cards stay on the local track.

DeepSeek V4 Pro is the price shock. Official DeepSeek API pricing puts cache-miss input at $0.435 and output at $0.87 per million tokens, with the same 1M context as the rest of the frontier table. Arena deepseek-v4-pro sits around 1457 Elo — low enough that prior weeks rejected it when the set floor was higher, but within the 25-point threshold of today's floor. It becomes helloai's Honest Daily Use leader: the default when token volume dominates and Mythos-class quality is not required.

The drops are pure set-size math under the six-model rule. Grok 4.5 was the lowest Elo entry at 1468 with Honest Daily Use leadership that DeepSeek now owns on cost; Kimi K3 at 1485 loses the Moonshot slot to free room for Alibaba's higher arena score. Neither lab vanished from the market — only from the curated recommend table. Teams still routing to Grok or Kimi can keep those APIs; /api/recommend will no longer surface them.

Open-weight admission is separate. gpt-oss-20b is Apache 2.0, ~21B total / ~3.6B active MoE, native MXFP4 around 16 GB, and 1317 Elo on Arena. On our budget two-GPU cluster it measured 53.73 tok/s — the fastest open-weight throughput we track — which is why it replaces Qwen3 8B rather than expanding past six local cards. The result is a frontier set that spans Anthropic, Meta, Alibaba, Google, and DeepSeek, plus an open-weight shelf that finally includes OpenAI weights without pretending a 2.8T Kimi dump fits a single GPU.

title: Muse Spark 1.2 Ships With Muse Code
excerpt: Meta ships Muse Spark 1.2 with Muse Code at the same $1.25/$4.25 rates. helloai bumps 1.1 to 1.2 at 1498 Elo — still the cheapest agentic pick.
content: Meta just upgraded its cheapest frontier API without raising the price. Muse Spark 1.2 landed on the Meta Model API and OpenRouter around August 5–6 at the same $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens that made 1.1 the budget agentic pick — still with a full 1M-token context window. On Arena's text overall board dated August 6, muse-spark-1.2 (xHigh) sits at 1498 Elo, second only to Claude Fable 5 at 1507 in helloai's tracked set.

The model did not arrive alone. Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said Spark 1.2 was developed and trained alongside Muse Code, Meta's first coding-agent product, now in preview with pay-as-you-go pricing described as similar to the Spark API. That pairing matters more than a version digit: Meta is selling a harness and a model as one stack, the same play Anthropic and OpenAI have been running with Claude Code/Cowork and Codex-style surfaces. For teams already on the Meta Model API, the path is a same-id upgrade, not a vendor switch.

helloai applies the same rule it uses for every same-provider bump: replace 1.1 with 1.2 under the existing muse id. Pricing and context do not change; the card copy and arena aliases do. Muse remains the cheapest agentic option we track, undercutting Opus 5 ($5/$25), Kimi K3 ($3/$15), and Grok 4.5 ($2/$6) on both sides of the meter for teams that want multi-agent orchestration without Mythos-class bills.

Trade-offs stay real. Arena votes for 1.2 are still early compared with Fable and the long-lived Claude Opus lines, and Meta's contributor tier — roughly $0.10/$0.20 when you opt in to training use of prompts and completions — is a different product from the standard no-train production rate. Standard tier is the default for anyone treating this as a production dependency. Coding-agent previews also move faster than public Elo; treat Muse Code claims as vendor-directed until your own harness evals land.

The wider board did not freeze while Meta shipped. Qwen3.8-Max is pressing the $2/$6 tier with high preliminary arena scores, and Gemini 3.5 Pro is still missing from Google's pricing page. For /api/recommend today, Meta's slot is 1.2: same budget, slightly higher human preference, and a coding-agent surface that did not exist when 1.1 replaced Qwen in July. The next decision is whether that stack holds once Alibaba's Max-class model and Google's delayed Pro both finish their launches.
